name: Huawei Ascend 950DT NPU (per-accelerator, Atlas 650E / 950 SuperPoD)
memory_bandwidth_basis: PER NPU, DERIVED BY DIVISION from the server figure: the Atlas 650E specification gives '8 x 96 GB total, 4.0 TB/s peak memory bandwidth', so each 950DT carries 96 GB at 4.0/8 = 500 GB/s. Huawei states the 4.0 TB/s server figure directly and does not publish a per-NPU breakdown; the division is arithmetic, not a claim. Note this is ON-CHIP memory, not HBM - Huawei describes it as 'Huawei's self-developed on-chip memory', which is a materially different memory technology from the HBM2e on the 910 generation and should not be compared to HBM3 bandwidth numbers without reading the vendor's wording. Source cn-huawei-atlas-650e-spec.

notes:
THE HIERARCHY POINT: this generation breaks the pattern that the whole 910 line was stuck in, and it does so in a way that matters specifically for inference. The per-NPU numbers are derived by dividing Huawei's server figures by 8 (Atlas 650E: 8 NPUs, 12.48 PFLOPS mxFP4, 6.43 PFLOPS mxFP8/FP8/HiF8, 3.40 PFLOPS FP16/BF16, 8 x 96 GB, 4.0 TB/s), giving roughly 1560 / 804 / 425 TFLOPS per NPU - note that FP8 is only 1.9x FP16 and mxFP4 only 3.7x FP16, which is a deliberately narrow precision ladder compared to Blackwell's roughly 2x-per-step. THAT is the important number for a serving study: the 4:1 FP16-to-FP4 spread means low-precision decode acceleration is worth much less here than on an NVIDIA part, and there is no FP4-with-FP8-accumulate story to tell. Everything quoted is a VENDOR THEORETICAL figure and Huawei's own page carries the disclaimer 'Theoretical computing power may have a <1% error in actual testing' - so these are clock-derived peak numbers, not measurements. The genuinely novel part is memory, not compute: 96 GB per NPU of Huawei-developed on-chip memory at 500 GB/s per NPU, and at SuperPoD scale '256 TB unified global memory addressing & memory semantics' across up to 1024 NPUs. UNIFIED GLOBAL MEMORY ACROSS 1024 NPUS IS THE HEADLINE. If real, it removes the tensor-parallel-collectives problem that constrains every GPU-based serving stack, because a KV cache can be addressed as one flat address space rather than replicated per rank - that is a fundamentally different memory model from NVLink domains and it is the first credible non-Apple unified-memory story in a datacenter part. Scale-up link is UB Link 2.0: 784 GB/s bidirectional per NPU intra-server, 1.68 TB/s per NPU in 16-NPU full-mesh, 1.72 PB/s across a 1024-NPU SuperPoD - which is roughly 1.7 TB/s per chip and therefore about 3.5x the local memory bandwidth, an unusually healthy scale-up-to-local ratio and the exact inverse of the 910B's HCCS problem. Scale-out is UBoE and RoCE at 400 Gbps per NPU unidirectional. Atlas 650E is 14U air-cooled at ~14.5 kW with 2 x 950 CPUs; Atlas 950 SuperPoD is a 44OU cabinet of 64 NPUs at ~100 kW liquid-cooled, and scales to 1024 NPUs. Software: MindIE on CANN (cn-huawei-mindie). Note the predecessor-generation comparison is not apples to apples: 910C used SMIC 7 nm and HBM2e, this uses on-chip memory, and Huawei does not publish a process node for 950DT.
MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: STILL NULL, AND HERE IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-04). %s NO FIGURE WAS BACK-COMPUTED FROM BANDWIDTH. That is the standing rule for this field in this repo and it was applied to every null here rather than to a subset: a width derived by dividing a published aggregate bandwidth by an assumed or half-assumed per-pin rate is two inferences stacked on one number, and if either inference is wrong the record looks populated while being wrong. The correct state of this field is 'the vendor does not publish it', and the note above names the specific document that was read and found not to carry it, so a future pass does not have to re-establish that from scratch.
